description:
fz has no `Access` module, so `Access.get/2` written longhand is unresolved.

  Access.get(%{a: 1}, :a)
    elixir  1
    fz      error[lower/unbound]: unresolved direct runtime callee `Access.get/2`

Until fz-5xp.4 this appeared to work, but only because the bracket-access decode
swallowed ANY alias whose called field was `get` and turned it into an index --
the same bug that swallowed every user-defined `get/2`. With the decode now
keyed on a front-door marker rather than the alias, the sugar is sound and the
missing module is visible.

A clean diagnostic is the right behaviour for a module that does not exist, so
this is not a regression. But Elixir code reaches for `Access` directly --
`Access.get/2`, `Access.fetch/2`, `get_in/2`, `put_in/3`, `update_in/3` -- and
`m[key]` is only the sugar over it.

Scope when taken: decide whether fz implements `Access` as a real module (an fz
protocol over map/keyword/struct, which is what Elixir does) or documents its
absence. Related: the bracket-index lowering itself assumes a map or struct
receiver and aborts on anything else -- see the bracket-access abort ticket.
title: fz has no Access module; Access.get/2 longhand is unresolved
